skill_protocol:
TECHNOLOGY COMPANY FORECASTING — STRICT BLIND EXECUTION CONTRACT

You must execute the same substantive workflow as the unified Skill.

1. Freeze contract: blind alias, cutoff, fiscal basis, GAAP, perimeter, horizons, output/readiness.
2. Evidence: E0 filing anchors; E1 official results/Q&A and customer/supplier official read-through may alter near drivers with execution discount; measured E3 research may alter a specific driver only after independent corroboration; E2 papers set feasibility/failure/regime tails and cannot directly create revenue/share/margin; E4 anonymous claims are monitor-only. Separate facts, calculations, assumptions and scenarios.
3. Review and explicitly report every source family: filings/results, formal investor dialogue, cross-company official, independent industry measurement, sell-side/deep research, named experts, technical papers/standards, news/media discovery. Record rejected and duplicated sources.
4. Source independence: repeated reports from the same original source count as one cluster. A company statement and an article repeating it are one cluster. Base changes need at least two independent clusters and at least one direct/official/measured source, a causal chain, adjustment cap and falsification trigger.
5. Normalize history/perimeter/GAAP. Do not infer future acquisitions or later outcomes.
6. Route 100% of economics to mechanisms without double count. For this case use recurring-contract software, backlog conversion, maintenance/renewal, services, hardware/IP timing, technical design-complexity adoption, GAAP operating leverage, and accounting-standard timing.
7. Demand/customer model: payer, paid usage/seat or contract base, retention/renewal, new bookings, price/mix, customer concentration, design activity and alternatives.
8. Delivery/supply model: software capacity is not usually binding, but product release, verification hardware, IP timing, support and skilled labor may be.
9. Formula model: Revenue = recurring opening base × retention × price/mix + new-booking conversion + services + hardware/IP timing. Backlog is visibility, not automatic growth. GAAP operating profit = gross profit − R&D − S&M − G&A − restructuring/acquisition items.
10. Produce FY+1/FY+2/FY+3 point and intervals, Bear/Base/Bull probabilities, breakpoints, monitoring and human-required gaps. Year 3 must have wider uncertainty.
11. Discuss cash/capital and normalized economics qualitatively even though valuation is not scored. Do not use peak economics as terminal. Include reverse/implicit expectations conceptually.
12. Red-team at least six substantive risks: evidence permission/leakage, customer/renewal, backlog conversion, hardware/IP timing, GAAP/accounting timing, double-counting, valuation/normalization, source independence.
13. Readiness cannot exceed retrospective blind research-grade. Return only the required JSON. Do not identify the company or use remembered future outcomes.

facts: FY0 revenue index=100; GAAP operating margin=16.67%; revenue grew 7.6%; prior margin 13.6%.
Product+maintenance 93.4%; services 6.6%. Approximately 90% of revenue recognized over contract life.
Backlog/FY0 revenue=138.9%; prior-year backlog/prior revenue=135.3%; management expected about 70% of FY+1 revenue from backlog.
R&D/FY0 revenue=41.4%. One reporting segment. Hardware and IP timing more volatile than recurring software.
sources.limits: backlog does not guarantee renewal, price or timing; product disclosure limited

facts: >100 digital/signoff customers; ~40 working at leading 7nm; >30 tapeouts; 20 full-flow competitive wins.
Management old-standard FY+1 revenue guide index 105.8–107.8. New accounting standard expected to reduce reported FY+1 revenue about 2% through contract timing.

facts: Large peer: ~88% revenue over time; backlog/revenue ~131%; annual revenue +12.5%; multi-year licenses, maintenance and IP are major sources.
Independent industry measurement: latest-quarter EDA revenue +8% YoY; four-quarter moving average +11.5%; broad category/geographic growth.

sources.limits: long-term demand boundary only; no direct company revenue/share
